Roll a D6 after the battle — on a score of 2+ the effect ends.; 4: Result Magical Shutdown: The wizard cannot cast any spells for the duration of this battle.; 5-6: Result Uh-oh! The spell has been cast successfully — upon the wizard himself! Any additional decisions are made by the wizard's left player.; 7: Result Pooh, nothing at all! Except for the spell's failure there are no further consequences.; 8-9: Result Magical Explosion: The wizard is thrown D6" in a random direction and then lands knocked down.; 10 — 11: Result Magical jam: The wizard cannot cast a spell in his next shooting phase. Missile weapons may be used as normal, of course.; 12: Result Wait, what's that? The uncontrollable powers of Chaos cause the wizard to mutate. After a moment of horror the transmutation ends. You may choose a free Mutation for the wizard chosen from the Possessed's Mutations chart (Mordheim Rulebook page 76).

strigos.name: Survivors of Strigos

units.name: Strigoi Vampire
units.sp: A Strigoi Vampire may not wield any weapons, as it relies upon brute strength, tooth and claw. They do not suffer from any penalties for fighting unarmed. Leader: Any models in the warband within 6" of the Strigoi Vampire may use his Leadership instead of their own. Kindred Hatred: A Strigoi Vampire Hates vampires of other blood-lines. Cause Fear: Vampires are terrifying Undead creatures and therefore cause Fear. Immune to Psychology: Vampires are not affected by psychology (such as fear) and never leave combat. Immune to Poison: Vampires are not affected by any poison. No Pain: Vampires treat a Stunned result on the Injury chart as Knocked Down.

units.name: Seer
units.sp: Seeker: Due to their premonitions, Seers who partake in a battle, and are not taken Out of Action may modify a single exploration dice by +/- 1. Wizard: Seers have one spell randomly generated from the Charms & Hexes spell list.

units.name: Domnu
units.sp: Child of Darkness: Borne of the night, Domnu are steadfast and loyal servants of the Strigoi. They are immune to the Spooky special rule for Sylvania. Gypsy Ward: Possessing an innate resistance to magic, the Domnu has a special save of 5+ versus magical attacks.

units.name: Ghoul
units.sp: Ghouls never carry any equipment, apart from a few bones which they use as primitive weapons. Cause Fear: Ghouls are twisted and repulsive creatures and therefore cause Fear.

units.name: Giant Bat
units.sp: Jaws and brutality. Animals: Giant Bats are animals and thus do not gain experience. Flying: Giant Bats fly through the night air, and thus do not need to climb or leap over gaps, even if their movement phase ends with them over open air. Large: Giant Bats are Large creatures. Sonic: Giant Bats use sonic vibrations to navigate the dark of night. No Line of Sight is needed for a charge.

strigos.rules:
Choice: Exactly 1 Strigoi Vampire, max. 1 Seer, max. 3 Domnu, max. 5 Strigany; any number of Ghouls, max. 2 Giant Bats.
Undead Leader: The Strigoi Vampire is the only Undead model in the warband. The warband does not disband if the Strigoi is killed, though it may not hire a new one.
Hired Swords: May hire the Hired Swords of an Undead warband.

vampirehunters.name: Vampire Hunters of Sylvania

units.name: Vampire Hunter
units.sp: Leader: Any models in the warband within 6" of the Vampire Hunter may use his Leadership instead of their own. Stake the Vampire!: A Vampire Hunter Hates Vampires. They must always move towards a Vampire on the field (if he can see them) unless he can shoot (in which case he may choose).

units.name: Priest of Morr
units.sp: Prayers of Morr: May perform the Funerary Rites, using the rules for Magic. As priests of Morr seldom engage in martial activities, they may only be armed with a Dagger and a Scythe as weapons. Priests of Morr may never wear Armour. Loner: Few people care to spend any length of time in the company of a priest of Morr — even when it is their duty to do so. As such, a priest of Morr is used to being alone and probably prefers it that way. Priests of Morr do not suffer from the All Alone rules. Funerary Rites: Priests of Morr are not wizards, however they do have numerous Funerary Rites which they may perform. As such, priests of Morr may randomly choose a Funerary Rite listed on the following page.

units.name: Slayer
units.sp: Stake the Vampire!: A Slayer Hates Vampires. They must always move towards a Vampire on the field (if he can see them) unless he can shoot (in which case he may choose).

units.name: Pilgrim
units.sp: Fanatical: A Pilgrim of Pain believes that the end of the world is nigh should the undead threat not be stopped. As such, nothing holds any terror for them in the mortal world. Pilgrims automatically pass any leadership-based tests they are required to take. A Pilgrim may never become a Warband leader. Blunt: Due to bludgeoning weapons having a much more profound effect upon the undead, Pilgrims ignore all bladed and ranged weapons in favor of maces, hammers and staffs. The only exception to this is the silver-tip stake, for it's incredible destructive powers against Vampires.

units.name: Wolfhound
units.sp: Jaws and brutality. A Wolfhound never use nor need weapons or armour. Animal: Wolfhounds are animals and thus do not gain experience.

vampirehunters.rules:
Choice: Exactly 1 Vampire Hunter, max. 1 Priest of Morr, max. 3 Slayers; any number of Villagers, max. 4 Pilgrims, max. 4 Wolfhounds.
Hired Swords: May hire the Hired Swords of a Human Mercenary warband. Vampire Hunters accept nearly all aid that is available.

amazonSkills.name: Amazon Skills
amazonSkills.note: Amazon Heroines (instead of the standard skill tables).
skills: Always strikes first in the first close-combat round against Skinks (regardless of who charged).
May re-roll one out-of-action roll after the battle (the second result stands).
Enemy in base contact: Ld test at the start of each turn, otherwise it cannot attack (defence only). Useless against Lizardmen/Undead.
+1 A when charging; immune to charm effects and fear.
Hidden in jungle terrain: Enemies halve the distance at which they can spot her.

tgSkills.name: Tomb Guardian Additional Skills
skills: Chariots are very difficult to control and a warrior must have this skill to drive a chariot effectively in combat. A charioteer without this skill cannot charge. The Tomb Lord may learn it although it is Academic (Mordheimer inconsistency, played by intent: he is the obvious charioteer).

pitSkills.name: Pit Fighter Skills
pitSkills.note: Pit Fighter Heroes (instead of the standard tables).
skills: Ignores the heavy-weapon penalty entirely — the Strength bonus (e.g. morning star) applies in every round.
On going OOA: Toughness test (−1 each subsequent round). On success he stands up and fights on (a 2nd OOA is final).
Ignores all "difficult to use" rules — may e.g. combine a morning star + buckler, or two morning stars.
Instead of a normal charge, a shoulder slam: one attack at +1 S, +1 to hit, no weapon bonuses, criticals on 5+.

cavalrySkills.name: Riding / Cavalry Skills
cavalrySkills.note: Mounted warriors (e.g. Imperial Outriders) with the Ride skill.
skills: Mounted leader: Leadership radius +6" (in addition to other bonuses).
Shooting against him −1; requires an Initiative test (otherwise loss of control). Not with heavy armour/shield/missile weapons.
When charging an unmounted enemy: one extra S4 attack.
Always strikes first in close combat against dismounted enemies.
Ride up to the mount's movement, then dismount at once (counts as a diving charge from 2").
Mount within 2" and immediately make a full move/charge.
Shoots at full gallop and in a 360° arc (additional −1 to hit).
Against mounted enemies: A wounded enemy model gets +1 on its "Whoa Boy!" table.

dthSkills.name: Dwarf Special Skills
dthSkills.note: Dwarf Heroes may use this list instead of any standard skill tables available to them.
skills: When using a weapon with the Parry rule he parries on an equal or higher roll (not just higher). With two parrying weapons he may parry up to two attacks; with two Dwarf axes he may re-roll failed parries.
When rolling on the Heroes' Serious Injury chart after being taken out of action, the dice may be re-rolled once (the second result must be accepted, even if worse).
When rolling on the Exploration chart at the end of a game, he may modify one dice by +1/−1.
When rolling on the Injury table for this Hero, 1–3 = knocked down, 4–5 = stunned, 6 = out of action.
3+ save on a D6 to avoid being stunned (treat as knocked down instead). With a helmet this save is 2+ (replaces the normal helmet rule).

arabSkills.name: Arab Special Skills
arabSkills.note: Arab Heroes may use this list instead of any standard skill tables available to them.
skills: Can bury himself in sand and become almost undetectable: may hide in open ground. Cannot be used inside buildings.
May run and shoot, but suffers −2 to hit instead of the −1 to hit for moving.
Weather conditions such as heat no longer affect this model.

bretSkills.name: Bretonnian Special Skills (Virtues)
bretSkills.note: Bretonnian Heroes may use this list instead of any standard skill tables available to them.
skills: His purity of heart resists enemy magic: any spell cast against the Knight is dispelled on a D6 roll of 4+.
Against a model with a higher Strength than himself, he may re-roll any failed to-hit rolls in close combat.
Once per game, if he is not out of action, stunned or knocked down, you may re-roll a failed Rout test.
Contempt for dishonourable weapons: subject to Hatred of all enemies armed with shooting weapons.
Eager to get to grips: May add +D3" to his move when charging (roll each time before moving).

deSkills.name: Dark Elf Special Skills
deSkills.note: Dark Elf Heroes may use this list instead of any standard skill tables available to them.
skills: May make a 4" follow-up move if he takes all of his opponents out of action.
May choose skills from the Strength table from now on. The Sorceress may never take this skill; no more than two warriors in the warband may have it at one time.
Avoids melee or missile attacks on a roll of 6; with Step Aside or Dodge this improves to 4+ in the relevant area.
Exactly the same as the Skaven skill.
If the Hero doesn't search for rare items, he may make D3−1 doses of Dark Venom instead (must be used in the next battle; cannot be sold or traded).

weSkills.name: Wood Elf Special Skills
weSkills.note: Wood Elf Heroes with the Special skill list may use this list instead of any standard skill tables available to them.
skills: An understanding of magic: 4+ saving throw against hostile magic.
The Elven gods favour him: Once per game he may re-roll any failed roll.
Can spot hidden enemy models up to 2× his Initiative in inches away.
Expert tracker: May modify the result of one exploration die by +/−1. Only one Elven Hero may possess this skill.
Always deployed last, anywhere out of sight of the enemy. If both players infiltrate, roll D6 — lowest deploys first.

skavenSkills.name: Skaven Special Skills
skavenSkills.note: Skaven Heroes may use this list instead of any standard skill tables available to them.
skills: Declare at the start of his turn: +1 attack and +D3" total move for the duration of his own turn, but suffers D3 S3 hits with no armour save at the end of the turn.
May wield a shield, knife or sword with his tail: an extra attack with the appropriate weapon, or a +1 bonus to his armour save.
Needs no Initiative test when climbing walls and other sheer surfaces.
Always placed after the opposing warband, anywhere out of sight and more than 12" from any enemy. If both players infiltrate, roll D6 — lowest sets up first.
Fights with bare paws without penalties and counts as having two weapons (+1 attack); causes critical hits on a To Wound roll of 5–6. With Fighting Claws: +2 attacks instead of +1.

pestilensSkills.name: Clan Pestilens Special Skills
pestilensSkills.note: Members of Clan Pestilens may choose these skills instead of the standard ones.
skills: As the Skaven skill: +1 attack and +D3" move for his turn; D3 S3 hits (no save) at the end of the turn.
Requires Black Hunger. Gains Frenzy; the only weapon he may use in close combat is a censer.
Immune to poisons and diseases; if taken out of combat by a failed censer test he does not roll for injuries (recovers automatically).

Requires Rotten Body. A model that takes the bearer out of action in close combat must take a Toughness test (D6): if the roll is higher than its Toughness it suffers an automatic wound (a 6 always wounds). Undead/Possessed never test.
Requires the Resilient skill. Treats Stunned injuries as Knocked Down.

slayerSkills.name: Troll Slayer Skills
slayerSkills.note: Dwarf Slayers may use this list as well as any standard skill tables available to them.
skills: May double his attacks in the turn he charges; suffers −1 to hit that turn.
Always wounds any opponent on a roll of 4+, regardless of Toughness (unless his own Strength would mean a lower roll is needed).
+1 to his close-combat to-hit rolls during the turn he charges.

pirateSkills.name: Pirate Special Skills
pirateSkills.note: Pirate Heroes may use this list instead of any standard skill tables available to them.
skills: At the start of his close-combat phase he may burst into song: one opponent in base contact must pass a Ld test or lose 1 Attack that turn. No effect on Undead or other non-living creatures (e.g. Possessed).
If he Falls, he may ignore the D3 hits on a single roll of 4+. If knocked down or stunned within 1" of a precipice, he may re-roll the Initiative test to avoid falling.
With a Sword he parries already on an equal roll (not just higher) — but only when not in the open (in cover, in a building, or within 2" of a terrain feature).
Captain only: Once per turn, one pirate within 8" who failed a test to flee combat (or to stop fleeing) may re-roll it. The Captain must be on his feet and not in close combat himself.
May ignore any Critical Hit on a roll of 5+ (the wound is then treated as normal).
At the end of any close-combat phase while in base contact with enemies, he may take a Ld test: If passed, he makes a normal move away (no run/charge) without the enemy striking blows.

norseSkills.name: Norse Special Skills
norseSkills.note: Norse Heroes with the Special skill list may use this list instead of the normal ones.
skills: When armed with a shield he may parry with it in addition to getting the 6+ save.
When armed with an axe or double-handed weapon, he may re-roll all failed to-hit rolls when he charges.
No enemy may parry an attack made by this hero — it strikes with such power that it pushes right through a buckler or sword.
Leader only: Models within 12" may use his Leadership (instead of the normal 6").
Never needs to take All Alone tests and may re-roll failed Fear tests.

swSkills.name: Shadow Warrior Special Skills
swSkills.note: Shadow Warrior Heroes may use this list instead of any standard skill tables available to them.
skills: Exactly the same as the Skaven skill: Always placed after the opposing warband, anywhere out of sight and more than 12" from any enemy. If both players infiltrate, roll D6 — lowest sets up first.
May always roll to charge opponents he cannot see (instead of the normal 4"), as long as he has the movement to reach them.
An enemy attempting to detect him while he is Hidden must halve its Initiative before measuring the distance.
If Hidden, may shoot or cast spells and remain Hidden. If the target is not taken out of action, it tests against its Initiative — on a success the Sniper is spotted and no longer hidden.
May choose skills from the Strength table from now on. Not for Shadow Weavers; only two members of the warband may ever have this skill at one time.

Shadow Weaver only: +1 to his Dispel roll with Elven Runestones. May also inscribe one warrior's gear with runes: that warrior may re-roll a single failed armour save or Parry once per battle (must be redone after each battle).

sosSkills.name: Sisters of Sigmar Special Skills
sosSkills.note: Sisters of Sigmar may use this list instead of the standard skill lists.
skills: Possessed or Undead opponents lose their first attack against the Sister in the first round of close combat (down to a minimum of 1).
Any spell which would affect her is nullified on a D6 roll of 4+. A nullified spell does not affect any other models either.
Matriarch only: May re-roll any failed Rout tests.
Hates all Skaven, Undead, Possessed, Beastmen, Dark Elves and any other evil warband (and all models in them). Non-Chaos humans who merely kill and loot are not included.
May re-roll any Fear tests and does not have to test if fighting alone against several opponents.

ostlanderSkills.name: Ostlander Special Skills
ostlanderSkills.note: Ostlander Heroes may use this list instead of any standard skill tables available to them.
skills: When charging, may attempt to knock down the opponent instead of his normal attacks: one to-hit roll at +1; no wound roll — on a hit the opposing model is Knocked Down.
Reeks of alcohol: All living enemies (not Undead/Possessed) are at −1 to hit him in close combat. May not carry open flames; fire attacks against him are at +1 Strength.

In the shooting phase, instead of shooting/casting: one visible enemy (LOS rules as shooting) takes a Ld test — if failed it must spend its next movement phase trying to get into close combat with the taunter.
'Normal' animals never attack him; up to two wardogs he owns do not count against the warband's maximum size.
Leader only: May re-roll a single Rout test once per game.

beastmenSkills.name: Beastmen Special Skills
beastmenSkills.note: Beastmen Heroes may use this list instead of the standard skill lists available to them.
skills: The Beastman's massively shaggy hide acts as armour: 6+ armour save that can be combined with other armour as normal.
The Beastman may buy one mutation (see the Possessed mutations).
Immune to fear and All Alone tests.
Mighty horns: May make an additional attack with his basic Strength in a turn he charges.
Beastman Chief only: May re-roll any failed Rout tests.
Affected by the rules of hatred when fighting any Human warbands.

orcSkills.name: Orc Special Skills
orcSkills.note: Orc Heroes (Orc Mob) may use this list instead of any standard list available to them.
skills: Special 3+ save on a D6 to avoid being stunned (treat as knocked down instead). With a helmet this save is 2+ (replaces the normal helmet rule).
Expert at bulldozing charges: May add +D3" to his charge range.
May ignore Fear tests when charging.
Boss only. The warband may re-roll any failed Rout test as long as the Boss is not out of action.
Thick, dark-green skin (possibly Black Orc blood): may add +1 to any armour saves.
Massive strength, aims at heads: any knocked down results the Orc causes in close combat count as stunned instead.

blackOrcSkills.name: Black Orc Special Skills
blackOrcSkills.note: Black Orc Heroes may use this list instead of the standard skill lists available to them.
skills: This young warrior has proven himself worthy of his Black Orc heritage. This skill may only be taken by a Young'un with the Black Orc blood ability and 25 experience. Once he gains this skill, the model is now considered a full Black Orc Warrior (yet still retains the title of Young'un). He follows all the rules for Black Orcs and uses their equipment list and has access to the same skill lists as a Black Orc.
Special 3+ save on a D6 to avoid being stunned (treat as knocked down instead). With a helmet this save is 2+ (replaces the normal helmet rule).
May add +D3" to his charge range.
May ignore Fear tests when charging.
Boss only. The warband may re-roll any failed Rout test as long as the Boss is not out of action.
Any knocked down results the Orc causes in close combat count as stunned instead.

hornedHunterSkills.name: Horned Hunter Special Skills
hornedHunterSkills.note: Horned Hunter Heroes may use this list instead of any standard list available to them.
skills: Masterful trap setter: Trip wire range extends to 4"; traps set by him trigger on 2+.
Always placed after the opposing warband, anywhere out of sight and more than 12" from any enemy. If both players infiltrate, roll D6 — lowest sets up first.
Reeks of alcohol and sweat: All living enemies (not Undead/Possessed) are at −1 to hit him in close combat. He may not carry open flames; fire attacks against him are at +1 Strength.
'Normal' animals (warhorses, warhounds, etc.) will never attack him; up to two wardogs he owns do not count against the warband's maximum size.
Roll one additional D6 during the exploration phase. A warband may only contain one pathfinder.
Crouches unseen in any cover: Enemies must halve their Initiative when attempting to find him while he is Hidden.

marauderSkills.name: Marauder Skills
marauderSkills.note: Marauders of Chaos Heroes (instead of the standard skill tables).
skills: The Hero counts as a Chaos Warrior: Uses the maximum profile for Warriors of Chaos (M4 WS8 BS8 S5 T5 W3 I8 A5 Ld9) and the Hero equipment list.
Leader only. The "Eye of the Gods" effect (Spawn/Mark) occurs already on 10+ (Norse leaders 11+).
If the Hero takes an enemy OOA with a double-handed weapon, he may immediately make an additional attack against another model in base contact. Requires Strongman.
The Hero buys a mutation (see Possessed mutations). May be taken more than once. With the Mark of Onogal, a Blessing of Nurgle instead (except the Mark of Nurgle).
Leader only. May re-roll failed Rout tests and is immune to fear and all-alone tests.

banditSkills.name: Bandit Special Skills
banditSkills.note: Hochland Bandit Heroes may use this list instead of any standard skill tables available to them.
skills: Instead of searching for rare equipment between games, roll a D6: 2-6 = D6+1 gold to the stash; on a 1 the robbery goes wrong (roll on the Serious Injury table as if taken Out of Action). Cannot be combined with the Huckster's Slick Operator.
An enemy trying to detect this warrior while he is Hidden must halve his Initiative (round up) before measuring the spotting distance.

If in close combat (and not knocked down/stunned) at the start of his Movement phase, the warrior may make an Initiative test to leave combat: success moves him 1" away (free) and he may then act normally; failure means he strikes last that round.
While Hiding, the warrior may shoot or cast spells and still remain Hidden — not when firing a black-powder weapon.
If an enemy tries to detect the Hidden bandit, roll a D6: on 4+ he stays undetected and Hidden.

lizardSkinkSkills.name: Lizardmen Skills (Skinks)
lizardSkinkSkills.note: Skink Heroes may use this list instead of a standard list.
skills: Expert at sneaking up on his prey: may set up anywhere on the table but no closer than 12" to an enemy, and must start the game in hiding.
Adept at making the most of cover: an additional −1 to hit the Skink while he is in cover (i.e. −2 in total).

lizardSaurusSkills.name: Lizardmen Skills (Saurus)
lizardSaurusSkills.note: Saurus Heroes may use this list instead of a standard list.
skills: His roar is so deafening that enemy models in base contact suffer −1 to hit in the first round of combat against him.
Years of battle have hardened his hide: he is only taken out of action on a 6+.

chaosDwarfSkills.name: Chaos Dwarf Skills
chaosDwarfSkills.note: Apprentice Sorcerer, Champions & Bull Centaur (instead of one of the standard tables).
skills: When rolling on the Injury table for this warrior, treat 1-3 as knocked down, 4-5 as stunned and only 6 as out of action.
After the battle the warrior may re-roll one of his Serious Injury results; the second result stands.
The warrior Hates all enemies (re-roll missed to-hit rolls in the first turn of every close combat).
3+ save on a D6 to avoid being stunned (a stun becomes knocked down instead). With a helmet this save is 2+ and replaces the normal helmet rule.

blackDwarfSkills.name: Chaos Dwarf Skills (Black Dwarfs)
blackDwarfSkills.note: Sorcerer & Gaolers (instead of one of the standard tables).
skills: After a game in which he was taken out of action, the Hero may re-roll once on the Serious Injury chart; the second result stands even if worse.
+3 when searching for Chaos Armour (incl. Mechanical Suits) or Obsidian Weapons, which he can craft himself; he ignores the Rarity and Gift of Chaos special rules. He may never wear Chaos Armour.
3+ save on a D6 to avoid being stunned (a stun becomes knocked down). With a helmet this is 2+ and replaces the normal helmet rule.
When rolling on the Exploration chart at the end of a game, the Hero may modify one dice by +1/−1.

Leader only. The leader may re-roll a failed Rout test (as long as he is not knocked down or stunned); the new result stands even if worse. If the leader is taken out of action the warband must make an immediate Rout test.
When rolling on the Injury table for this Hero, treat 1-3 as knocked down, 4-5 as stunned and only 6 as out of action.

battleMonkSkills.name: Battle Monk Skills
battleMonkSkills.note: Emissary & Dragon Monks (instead of a standard table). The Emissary may only ever pick Warmonger.
skills: If fighting unarmed, the Hero may reduce his Attacks by −1 to gain +1 Strength in close combat. He may sacrifice any number of attacks this way.
The monk may triple his Movement when running or charging, and may run even when there are enemy models within 8".
Cannot be intercepted while charging. He may escape from combat by leaping away without an Ld test and may declare a leaping charge in the same turn.

If two or more models are in close combat with the monk, he may pass an Initiative test (after the first attacks, before the second) to grab the first model as a shield — the second model's attacks are then directed at that grabbed model instead.
The Emissary may take an Ld test before the battle; if passed, D3+1 Raging Peasants join for that game (may exceed the maximum). Each Peasant is then subject to Hatred for the battle.

chapelKnightSkills.name: Knightly Skills
chapelKnightSkills.note: Bretonnian Chapel Guard Knights (instead of the standard tables).
skills: The Knight may learn one Virtue from the Bretonnian Knight Virtues list. Renowned Virtue may only be taken once.
Questing Knight only. When charging, charged by, or in combat with a fear-causing enemy, he may re-roll any one Leadership test (including Rout tests), accepting the second result.
Each turn the Knight may make one extra attack with a shield or kite shield, made at −1 Strength and treated as a club.
The Knight keeps the +1/+2 Strength bonus from Flails and Morning Stars after the first round of combat.

Ignores movement penalties for wearing armour while on foot. Strength, axes, critical hits and similar modifiers cannot reduce his armour save below 5+, nor can it be ignored by any non-magical means.

cavalcadeSkills.name: Cursed Cavalcade Special Skills
cavalcadeSkills.note: Cursed Cavalcade Heroes may use these skills instead of any of the standard skill tables available to them.
skills: Immune to fear, and stomps knocked-down opponents with his iron-shod boots: one additional attack at his own Strength against knocked-down opponents.
Any model wounded (and not saved) in close combat by this Hero loses 1 point of Strength permanently for the rest of the battle.
At the end of each close combat phase, the Duelist may force a non-large opponent he fights one-on-one to pass a Strength test or be pushed 2" in a direction of the Duelist’s choice.

ogreSkills.name: Ogres Special Skills
ogreSkills.note: Maneaters Heroes (instead of the standard lists).
skills: The Ogre may wield a Difficult to Use weapon and a hand weapon at the same time (but not two Difficult to Use weapons).
May unleash thunderous fumes on all enemies engaged with him: those that fail an Ld test suffer −1 to hit for the turn. He must wait until a new enemy engages him before doing it again.
Immediately learn one skill from the Shooting or Academic lists (once only; not available to the Mountain Guide).
When charging, may make a single attack at +1 to hit instead of his normal attacks; if it hits, the target is automatically knocked down.
Leader only. The warband may hire Hired Swords available to Mercenaries; if the leader dies, all such Hired Swords are removed.
Leader only. Re-roll the first failed Rout test of each battle.

merchantSkills.name: Merchant Special Skills
merchantSkills.note: Merchant Caravans Merchant (instead of the standard lists).
skills: Whenever a Rout test is required, the Merchant may pay 5 gc per non-Hero member still in the game; if he does, one already-out-of-action member does not count for that Rout test. Repeatable while gold lasts.

If the Merchant was not taken out of action, before the trading phase he may take an Ld test: On a pass the warband gains 1 gc per Experience point the Merchant has; on a fail it loses up to that amount.
If not taken out of action, the Merchant may search for D3+1 rare items after each battle instead of one.
+1 on the roll to see what an item fetches when selling via the Trade special rule.
Instead of searching for rare items, the Merchant may visit the black market for special items (Dispel Scroll, Lesser Artefact, Magical Artefact, Magical Scroll); such items can never be sold back.

ngSkills.name: Night Goblin Special Skills
ngSkills.note: Night Goblin Heroes (instead of any standard list).
skills: Adds +6" to the range of any missile weapon he uses (nets excluded).
Big Boss only. After all other deployment, he may move D3 of his warband members.
Set up after the opposing warband, anywhere out of sight and more than 12" from any enemy. If both sides infiltrate, roll D6 each — lowest sets up first.

'Chuck and charge': Declare a net charge and throw a net at the target. If it hits and the target fails to escape, the target counts as knocked down and the Goblin completes the charge; otherwise it is a failed charge (stop 1" away).

restlessSkills.name: Restless Dead Special Skills
skills: Secretly nominate one Zombie as a Corpse Bomb. If it charges or is charged it detonates: all models within D6" take D3 Strength 4 hits, and the Zombie is destroyed. Corpse Bombs killed by shooting do not detonate. Only one at a time (Liche and Necromancer may both take this skill).
At the start of the battle deploy D3 Zombies for free. They do not count toward the maximum warband size (but add to rating), cannot be Corpse Bombs and last only for the battle.

Instead of his normal attacks, make one unarmed Wraith Touch: If it hits it wounds automatically. A Liche that wounds with it regains one lost wound (not above its starting total); Necromancers do not. No effect on the Possessed or Undead.
If the hero did not search for rare items in the last exploration phase, he starts the next battle with a pool of D3+1 modifiers (+1) he may add to his casting rolls, as many at a time as he wishes.
The maximum warband size is increased by 1.

dwSkills.name: Dreamwalkers Special Skills
dwSkills.note: Dreamwalkers Heroes with access to Special Skills may use the following list:
skills: When a Dreamer proves to be a brave leader and truly chosen of Morr, his followers will follow their dreamer to death with unwavering courage. To represent this, Morr Worshwishpers can use the dreamer's lead if they are 12" away instead of the usual 6". (Only for Dreamer).

The dreamwalkers are convinced that they are the chosen ones to carry out Morr's will and eradicate the necromantic plague of the old world. Once per game, if the Dreamer is not out of action, stunned or knocked down, you may re-roll a failed rout test. (Only for Dreamer).
Only the true faithful followers of Morr know and accept death and become inured to horror. The model is immune to Fear, and need never take All Alone tests.

The hero has been blessed by Morr and has his protection against the magic that his enemies cast against him. Any spell that could affect the model is nullified with a D6 roll of +4 when fighting the undead. Note that if the spell is nullified, it does not affect this model, but it does affect any other model as it normally would.

drSkills.name: Druchii Special Skills
drSkills.note: Druchii Heroes may use the following Special Skills in addition to any normally available to them:
skills: The Dark Elf is infused with an intense raging thirst for blood and is a whirlwind in hand-to-hand combat, moving from opponent to opponent. The Druchii may make a 4" follow up move if they take all of their opponents out of action. If the elf comes into contact with another enemy, this starts a new combat. This new combat takes place in the following turn and the model counts as charging.

Few can ever hope to match an Elf's inhuman quickness and agility. An Elf with Fey Quickness can avoid melee or missile attacks on a roll of 6. If the Elf also has Step Aside or Dodge, this will increase to a 4+ in the relevant area. For example, an Elf with Fey Quickness and Step Aside avoids melee attacks on a 4+ and missile attacks on a 6.
The Dark Elf can Infiltrate. This skill is identical to the Skaven skill.

The Dark Elf is proficient in concocting different poisons. If the Hero doesn't search for rare items, he may make D2 doses of Dark Venom instead. The poison must be used in the next battle and cannot be sold or traded to other warbands as the Dark Elves guard their secrets very carefully.

Eyes of this hero are so keen and hands so steady that he can completely omit the penalty for long range if using a crossbow type weapon. Further, if he did not move this turn, he can shoot from repeater crossbow twice per turn without penalty or three times per turn with −1 penalty to hit.

Naggaroth is a harsh land with harsh inhabitants and weaklings are shown no mercy. This elf is able to survive by pure strength of will. If the model gets out of action and result of the Serious Injuries roll is death, make a Leadership test against unmodified Ld of the model (no holy relics etc.). If you succeed, the model will survive but will miss D3 battles instead.

There are numerous legends detailing the excellent eyesight of the Elves, both Druchii and Asur kin. This elf can spot Hidden enemies from twice as far away than normal warriors (i.e. twice his Initiative value in inches).

scSkills.name: Dwarf Slayer Cult Special Skills
skills: The hero is completely immune to all psychology and never need to test if fighting alone. [Stubbles and Axe Hurlers Only. See 'Stubbles' and "Axe Hurlers" for details.] Slayers Only
The Slayer may double his attacks on the turn in which he charges. He will suffer a −1 'to hit' penalty on that turn. Slayers Only

In close combat, the Slayer always wounds any opponent on a roll of 4+, regardless of Toughness, unless his own Strength (after all modifiers due to weapon bonuses, etc) would mean that a lower roll than this is needed. Slayers Only.
The Slayer may add +1 to his close combat 'to hit' rolls during the turn in which he charges. Slayers Only.

If the Hero is taken out of action in hand-to-hand, he may immediately make the remainder of his attacks before being removed, if he hasn't made all of his attacks already this turn. He may use this skill if he is knocked down or stunned. Slayers Only.

If the Hero charges a model but the charge fails, the Hero may still move the full distance of his move. This skill may only be used against enemies within sight or that the Slayer can detect. Slayers Only.

The Hero is well taught in the hand-to-hand arts of axemanship. He may reroll all missed attacks if he was using an axe or a dwarven axe in the hand-to-hand phase of the turn that he charges. May not be used with Whirling Blades.
Dwarfs are hardy individuals and this Hero is hardy even for a Dwarf! When rolling on the Injury table for this Hero, a roll of 1-3 is treated as knocked down, 4-5 as stunned, and 6 as out of action.
The Hero has a thick skull, even for a Dwarf. He has a 3+ save on a D6 to avoid being stunned. If the save is made, treat a stunned result as knocked down instead.

A Bard's rousing war songs steel the hearts of all those around him. Any friendly model within 6" of a Bard may re-roll any failed Leadership test with a +1 to Leadership, to a max of 10. This includes rout tests. Rememberer only.
In the postgame, if one or more Slayers in your warband died, all heroes and henchmen gain +1 Experience. Rememberer only.

grSkills.name: Grave Robbers Special Skills
grSkills.note: Grave Robber Heroes with access to Special skills may choose from the following list instead of any standard skill tables.
skills: The warrior is accustomed to darkness and has almost cat-like sight. Ignores All Alone tests and may double his Initiative when looking for Hidden models.

Having experienced countless encounters with the Undead, this warrior is hardened to terror. When charged by any Undead models, he does not have to take a Fear test. Additionally, he may nominate one of his attacks to Strike First.
The warrior is adept at fighting animated corpses. He ignores the No Pain rule for Undead and may stun them as normal.
Veteran of many grave-robbing escapades, the warrior is completely immune to all diseases and poisons.

This warrior is skilled at salvaging the bodies of the dead for profit. On a 4+, you may recover the body (and gear) of a friendly model slain in the Serious Injury phase. You may also attempt to do the same for enemy models by comparing Initiative rolls between the Body Dealer and enemy leader (or their most experienced model). On a tie, nothing is recovered; if the enemy wins, your Body Dealer is captured.

hfSkills.name: Halfling special skills
hfSkills.note: All Halflings may choose from the following special skills.
skills: The halfling as adept at staying as quiet as a mouse whilst hiding. Enemy warriors must use half their initiative value in inches (rounded down) when trying to detect this hidden halfling.

Having eaten a meal or six, this halfling may release a withering belch to distract his enemies. During the first round of hand to hand combat the halfling can release his noxious fumes upon all enemies within base contact. All enemies effected must take a leadership test. If the leadership test is failed then the putrid odor has severely affected the warrior's fighting ability and he must miss his first attack (regardless of whether he has only one attack or not).

This old halfling is greatly respected by the other members of the warband and they never question his word. All halflings may also re-roll any failed leadership test when within 6" of the leader as well as using his leadership for both tests.
The Halfling Thief can hide even after running, and can run while within 8" of enemy models if he starts and ends his move hidden.

The halfling has been hunting things ever since he was young (the more food he has, the better!) and has become well adapted to firing as silently and discreetly as possible. To represent this a Halfling may try and fire a ranged weapon and remain hidden. When shooting from hiding roll D6. On a 3+ the Halfling has managed to keep his actions inconspicuous to the eye of the enemy and may remain hidden that turn. Note this skill may not be combined with black powder weapons, they are just too noisy!

The Halfling has gained mountains of flab during his vast experience of eating fine foods and his thick bulk could swallow a sword whole! The Halfling always has a basic saving throw of 6 regardless of the enemy warrior's strength and on top of any armour he already wears.

The halfling has long-been skirting in the shadows, avoiding unwanted attention. So nimble is he that he may surprise even those who believe they've got them dead-to-rights. The halfling gains a bonus attack when charged that strikes first.

mhSkills.name: Masters of Horror Special Skills
mhSkills.note: The following skill list may be used by the Mad Scientist instead of the standard skill lists. Lunatic is available to all Heroes.
skills: The Mad Scientist can attempt to operate upon an injured minion. Reroll one dice of a single injury roll. You must accept the second roll.
The Mad Scientist fancies himself an alchemist and brews all sorts of concoctions and potions to guzzle down prior to battle. Roll a D6 at game-start and consult the following table

The Mad Scientist has gone above and beyond the understanding of most men, and has gained the ability to recreate life from death. Simply animating meat-puppets who parody life has bored him; he has moved on to reanimating dead cells. Any zombies within the warband now gain exp as normal human henchmen.
Giving in to ones insanity is quite rewarding. The model causes Fear and may reroll any Leadership Test.

ncSkills.name: Necrarchs Special Skills
ncSkills.note: Necrarch Vampire and Thrall Heroes with access to Special Skills may use the following list:
skills: Delving further into the evil teachings of Nagash, the Necrarch Vampire brings greater darkness to the realm of the living. He may roll immediately on the Scrolls of Nagash for a spell, and choose to do so again instead of a future Skill.
Such is the power of the Necrarch that the range of all his magical workings is extended by half-again.

So strong is the center of undeath within the Necrarch that he may save his constructs around him from their demise. As long as the Necrarch is within 4 inches of an undead henchman, they may only be taken Out of Action on a roll of a natural 6. Available only to the Leader.

npSkills.name: Nippon Special Skills
npSkills.note: Nippon Warband members may choose to use the following skill list instead of the standard skill lists.
skills: Defiance echoes through the ruins as a Nipponese warrior stares into the abyss of defeat. Once per grim engagement, when fate decrees their demise in the swirling melee, they unleash a final barrage of strikes before the void claims them. If these last, desperate blows fell an adversary, the warrior defies death's grasp, standing amidst the carnage with but a single thread of life remaining. If this model would be removed from the battlefield as the result of a close combat attack, before removing it make a single close combat attack with them as normal.

Stealth is their ally, the cloak of darkness their refuge. Skulking amidst the rubble, this shadow-clad warrior remains unseen, a specter haunting the twilight. Beyond the reach of distant foes, concealed behind shattered remnants of once-majestic edifices, they evade the enemy's gaze, a predator in the gloom. This Skill may only be taken by the Shinobi. This model is able to run while remaining hidden, as per hiding rules

Swift as the striking serpent, the Nipponese warrior answers the call to arms with deadly precision. When the enemy's charge shatters the silence, they retaliate with a lightning-quick strike, their blade singing the song of vengeance. In that fleeting moment, the strike-first rule bends to their will, delivering swift retribution to those who dare to assail them. When this model is charged they gain +1A that they may only use against the charger. This additional attack will 'strike first'. If the wielder is simultaneously charged by two or more opponents they will still only receive a total of +1A. These attacks are resolved at the Strength value of the model, with no further modifiers.

Alone they stand, surrounded by the whispers of the fallen and the specters of despair. Yet, in the face of overwhelming odds, the spirit of the Nipponese warrior remains unbroken. When the tempest of fear threatens to engulf them, they steel themselves against its icy grip. The solitary warrior defies the darkness, their resolve unyielding, bolstered by the ghosts of fallen comrades. If this model would normally take an all-alone test, it may be re-rolled, in addition, at the start of this models turn, if it is 6" away from friendly models, it can choose to have +1 to WS or BS until the start of its next turn.

Amidst the ruins, this warrior's serene rituals grant solace and insight. Forgoing treasure, they invest in reflection, seeking growth with a calming cup. After a battle, if this hero survives and did not go out of action, they can forgo searching for rare items and spends 10 gold crowns representing the cost of preparations for the tea ceremony. Then, Choose any other hero, and roll a D6. on a 3+, the chosen hero gains an Experience point from the introspective nature of the ceremony.

In the crucible of war, the favor of the divine grants protection to the faithful. Blessed by unseen forces, the Nipponese warrior defies the jaws of death itself. With the whispered blessings of the Kami, they rise from the brink of oblivion, their wounds miraculously mended, their spirit unbroken by the ravages of fate. When rolling on the Heroes Serious Injury chart for this Hero after a game in which he has been taken out of action, the dice may be re-rolled once. The result of this second dice roll must be accepted, even if it is a worse result.

ohSkills.name: Ogre Hunting Party Special Skills
ohSkills.note: Crude Belch: Ogres and Gnoblars eat almost anything. Consequences are to be expected from those inconsiderate enough to consume a rich meal before battle. A Hero with this 'condition' may unleash his noxious fumes on all enemies engaged in close combat. Those that do not pass a Ld test suffer a −1 'to hit' modifier for the turn. The Hero must wait until a new enemy engages him in combat before he relieves himself again. Scent Hound: The Ogre or Gnoblar has the keen nose of an expert tracker. The hero spots Hidden enemies from two times as far away as other warriors (ie, twice his Initiative value in inches). Sabre Trainer: Whenever a Sabretusk cub rolls a 1 for Untamed, if it started the turn within 6" of this hero, you may move the cub 3D6" towards any model within 12" of it that it can see (instead of towards the nearest model). Maneater (Ogres only): Ogre Hunters shun the companies of others, but they do travel far and wide, observing other the customs and skills of other cultures from afar . This Ogre may immediately learn one skill from the Shooting or Academic skill lists. This skill may be taken only once. Ogres only. Bull Charge (Ogres only): Ogres learn to use their vast bulk in a charge, trampling the enemy to the ground. When charging, an Ogre with this skill may attempt a single attack with a +1 'to hit' modifier rather than making his normal attacks. If successful the enemy model is automatically knocked down. Ogres only. Bellowing Roar (Leader only): An Ogre leader expects challenges to his authority. One of the best ways to suppress a mutineer in the ranks is to give his ear drums a good pounding. This skill may only be taken by the warband leader, allowing him to reroll the first failed Rout test. Ogres only. Set Traps (Gnoblars only): Trappers are experts at dropping snares. A Trapper may set a trap if he spends a turn doing nothing else (he may not set traps if he's just recovered from being Knocked Down). Place a marker in base contact with the Trapper. When another model, friend or foe, moves within 2" of the marker he risks setting off the trap: roll a D6. On a score of 3+ he has triggered the trap and suffers a S4 hit (note that the Trapper won't trigger his own traps). If the trap did not wound the model, the injured model has multiple wounds, or it didn't trigger, the 'victim' may finish his move- However, if the model was knocked Down or Stunned, place him 2" from the marker. Regardless whether the trap was triggered or not, the marker is removed. Gnoblar only. Infiltration (Gnoblars only): A Gnoblar with this skill is always placed on the battlefield after the opposing warband and can be placed anywhere on the table as long as it is out of sight of the opposing warband and more than 12" away from any enemy model. If both players have models which infiltrate, roll a D6 for each, and the lowest roll sets up first. Gnoblar only. Netter (Gnoblars only): Each game, the hero starts with 3 Nets. These may not be sold, traded, or given to another warrior- if not used during the game, they assumed to be stashed away or fallen apart. The next game, the hero will start with 3 nets, without penalty or cost. Gnoblar only.

psSkills.name: Protectorate of Sigmar Special Skills
psSkills.note: Protectorate Heroes with access to Special Skills may use the following list:
skills: The pious has been blessed by the Church. Any spell which would affect him is nullified on a D6 roll of 4+. Note that if the spell is nullified it will not affect any other models either.

Such is the faith of the warrior that there is little room for doubt or hesitation in his actions. When the opportunity arises to smite evil, one must be able to strike! As such, the warrior is hardened and immune to Fear.
Only the Warrior Priest may have this skill, which allows him to re-roll any failed Rout tests.

Only the Warrior Priest may have this skill. The Warrior Priest bellows his prayers to Sigmar, beseeching his protector to lend he and his men the strength to forge onwards. A Rousing Sermon must be declared at the beginning of a player's turn. The Warrior Priest and all friendly models within 6" gain +1 attack during that Hand to Hand combat phase. There may only be one Rousing Sermon per game.
With the blessed hand of Sigmar guiding his aim, the warrior lets loose his arrow. He may freely choose his target, and not only the closest enemy when declaring ranged attacks.

cmSkills.name: Skaven of Clan Moulder Special Skills
cmSkills.note: Clan Moulder heroes may choose to use the folowing Skill list instead of any of the standard Skill tables available to them.
skills: The Skaven can draw upon the dreaded Black Hunger, the fighting frenzy which gives him unnatural strength and speed but can ravage him from the inside. The Clan Moulder Hero may declare at the beginning of his turn that he is using this skill. The Hero may add +1 attack and +D3" to the total move on his profile for the duration of his own turn, but will suffer D3 S3 hits with no armour save possible at the end of the turn.

*A Clan Moulder hero with this skill has developed such an affinity for the horrific creatures under their dominion that the range at which any Beast/Animal Handling skills operate is doubled to 12". This applies to any and all such skills the character has and any they take in future.

The Hero has a scent that is particularly compelling to animals of all kinds, inspiring within them a desire to obey him. Any animal or beast from an opposing warband wishing to charge him must pass a Leadership test to do so unless said charge is the result of Goading. Mounts are assumed to be sufficiently under the control of their riders as to make them immune to the effect.

The Hero has become so adept with the Thingcatcher that even intelligent and nimble creatures such as Humans cannot escape him. If a Hero with this skill and equipped with a Thingcatcher takes an opposing model out of action, do not roll for injuries post-battle, instead treat the enemy as if they'd rolled Captured on the Serious Injuries chart. Large creatures such as Ogres cannot be caught in this way, but animals can.

* Stormvermin only Accidental exposure to raw warpstone or the experimental attentions - welcome or otherwise - of a Clan Moulder superior has resulted in this Hero developing some monstrous but useful mutation. Upon taking this skill the Hero must buy a Mutation from the list in the Mordheim Rulebook (see Possessed Warband) at half the listed cost.

snSkills.name: Snotling Special Skills
snSkills.note: The Bullied Goblin and Snotling Heroes may use the following Skill table instead of any of the standard skill tables available to them.
skills: When the hero with Stampede charges an opposing warrior, keep track of any other Snotlings that charged that same warrior this turn. You may have one of those charging Snotlings forfeit his attack in order to give the Stampeding Hero +1 Strength for each Base Attack forfeited (Example: a Snotling BigSnot with S2 and Stampede charges an opponent—he has a Snotling Mob charge with him. The Mob forfeits it's attack, granting the BigSnot +3 Strength; +1 S for each of the Mob's Base attacks (do not count additional hand attacks)). This bonus lasts until the end of the turn, and may be used multiple times (i.e. you may have multiple snotlings each forfeit their attack, each adding +1 S for each attack). However, each snotling may only forfeit his attack once per turn (thus, if you have two Stampeding heroes, you cannot have 1 snotling runt forfeit his attack TWICE, giving the bonus to two different warriors). A Snotling that forfeits his attacks forfeits them ALL—he may not choose to give up "half" his attacks or any other fraction. A Hero's Strength may not be increased beyond Strength 10.

Your Snotling always causes Critical Hits on rolls of 6 (when wounding) regardless of opponent's toughness. In addition, when combined with the Stampede charge attack, on any successful rolls to wound of 5+, the opponent gains no armour save.

(Scout and Promoted Runts Only) The Snotling is a master of fitting through small spaces and cracks in solid walls as well as burrowing under doors and floors. During the movement phase, you can declare that the Snotling is moving through a wall (even charging, if you can see/detect the target.) Roll a D6... on anything but a 1, your Snotling squeezes through and can attack as normal. On a 1, he has charged the wall blindly and not found a crevice, concussing himself in a cartoony manner. He cannot move again this turn and counts as knocked down if attacked in close combat. This Skill cannot be combined with the "Stampede" skill above.

(BigSnotz only) The BigSnot is immensely Big and strong, especially by Snotling standards. The BigSnot immediately learn ONE Strength Skill. A BigSnot may only take this skill once each. Cannot be combined with the skill "Frustratingly Tiny".

(Snotlings Only) Your Snotling is a master of using his tiny size to his advantage. In Hand-to-hand combat, enemies attacking your hero are at −1 to hit. Also, all opponents halve their Initiative when trying to detect a Hidden "Tiny" hero. This skill cannot be combined with the "Big Bully" skill above.

The Hero is a Master at controlling and leading the Snotlings around him as a Mob. So long as your Hero is within 2" of a Snotling Mob, both he and the Snotling Mob become Immune to Pscychology exactly as if the Hero counted as a second Snotling Mob. When this skill is combined with the "Stampede" skill above, the Hero automatically gains +1 to hit for each forfeited attack, in addition to +1 Strength. A natural roll of 1 will always fail to hit.

stSkills.name: Survivors of Strigos Special Skills
stSkills.note: Heroes with access to Special Skills may choose from the following lists:
skills: The following skill list may be used by the Strigoi Vampire instead of the standard lists. Iron Sinews: After death the Vampire's muscles grow far greater than they ever could have in his mortal life. The Strigoi becomes a beast of pure muscular power. Add +1S to the Vampire's profile. Great Thirster: Such is the appetite of this beast that he must feed almost constantly. Once the taste of blood has touched his lips, there is little that can stop the Vampire from drinking again. Once the Vampire takes a model Out of Action, treat him as Frenzied. This effect remains until he is Knocked Down, Stunned, or taken Out of Action. Curse of the Revenant: So strong is the desire for some to continue living that they defy death. Once a Vampire has taken the Great Thirster special skill, he may choose the Curse of the Revenant. This skill allows the Vampire to regenerate lost wounds on a D6 roll of 5+. Only one wound may be recovered in this fashion per turn. Dark Arts: The Strigoi has retained some of its former magical aptitude. He may choose Arcane Lore as an advance, and immediately roll for a spell on the Dark Arts table below. Subsequent spells may be chosen instead of skills.

The following skill list may be used by Strigany Heroes instead of the standard lists. Strigoi Vampires may not use this list. Light Fingers: Gypsies are apt to find things that others have lost. Should a Hero with this skill take an enemy model Out of Action, they will find an extra piece of Wyrdstone. Only one piece of treasure may be found in this manner per game. Practiced Arm: Such is the skill with which the Gypsy can launch throwing knives that he can throw two of them per turn. These missiles must be at the same target and gain +1 to their injury rolls to represent the skill with which they were aimed.

vhSkills.name: Vampire Hunters of Sylvania Special Skills
vhSkills.note: Vampire Hunters and Slayers may use the following skill list instead of the standard skill lists. The Priest of Morr may choose Blessing of Morr and Thirst for Vengeance as well as his normal skills. Iron Will: Such is the work of Slayers that there is little room for hesitation. When the opportunity arises, one must be able to strike! As such, the warrior is hardened and immune to Fear. Righteous Aura: Carrying many talismans from various gods, the warrior heads into battle assured of victory. Possessed or Undead opponents lose their first attack against the warrior in the first round of hand-to-hand combat (down to a minimum of 1). Thirst for Vengeance: The warrior Hates all undead. In his quest for revenge, he gains +1 attack in a turn where he has charged. Blessing of Morr: The warrior has the Death god's blessing in his work. Add +1 to all injury rolls against the undead. Touch of Darkness: Long has the Slayer been dealing in death. Perhaps too long. Due to his heightened intuition, he ignores darkness penalties.
